subject: SSO migration impact & compliance platform procurement
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.m@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.p@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.k@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.b@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: SSO migration impact on our compliance platform shortlist

Team —

We just got the Okta go-ahead for the org-wide SSO migration (timeline below). Before we commit to a renewal or new purchase for our compliance tooling (Vanta / TrustCenter), I want to surface integration and data-retention impacts so we don't end up with unexpected migration work post-contract.

Quick context:
- Okta migration kickoff: 2027-06-01 (pilot) -> org-wide by 2027-07-15
- Current compliance vendors: evaluating Vanta and TrustCenter (PoC complete, pricing in flux)

Questions I want answered by next week:
1) Which vendor supports Just-In-Time (JIT) provisioning with Okta and how much work for SCIM mapping?
2) Will SSO break any existing evidence upload automations or audit log collection?
3) Any contractual requirements for re-onboarding, audit windows, or data export timelines we should negotiate?

Attached: sso-migration-impact-notes.txt (quick checklist).

Can you both take initial ownership on items 1–2, and loop in security/legal for item 3? I can take point on vendor pricing / procurement coordination.

Thanks —
Rishi
Head of Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica.p@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.m@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.k@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.b@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SSO migration impact on our compliance platform shortlist

Rishi —

Thanks for the note. I ran the pilot checklist against both vendors and summarized findings below. High-level: both have Okta adapters, but the integration depth is different.

Vanta:
- SCIM provisioning supported; expects a single group-per-application pattern.
- Evidence collection: API hooks for logs and cloud connectors; we currently use a homegrown connector that will need minor changes (token refresh + new Okta API endpoints).
- No charge for re-onboarding in their standard SOW, but professional services (PS) recommended for SCIM mapping (~3 days).

TrustCenter:
- SCIM supported but with non-standard attribute mappings for role metadata — they'll require a mapping table and PS (~5 days).
- Their audit log ingestion expects a static service account; Okta's new session tokens may require rotating keys or a short-lived token approach.
- Contract: 60-day notice for major reconfiguration assistance; there is a fee schedule in their TS.

Action items I propose:
- Neha: confirm whether our audit log retention policy (90 days hot, 2 years cold) is compatible with both vendors' ingestion models.
- Laura: if legal can pre-clear re-onboarding language that caps PS time and cost, we can bake that into the purchase order.
- Rishi: continue procurement conversations and request a sample SCIM attribute map from both vendors.

I attached a quick matrix (I can upload as spreadsheet if useful).

—Monica
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Vanta Sales <sales@vanta.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.m@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.p@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 14:23:00 -0400
Subject: Re: SSO migration impact on our compliance platform shortlist

Hi Rishi / Monica,

Thanks for the heads up — quick answers from our integration team:

- SCIM: We fully support SCIM 2.0 and JIT provisioning. We attach an integration matrix showing required Okta attributes and an estimated PS scope. (Attachment: Vanta_SSO_integration_matrix.xlsx)
- Evidence collection: No change to majority of connectors. For Okta system logs, we use a webhook-to-ingestion pattern; the main work is pointing the webhook to our ingestion endpoint and validating event signatures.
- Contract: We'll include one complimentary re-onboarding session for migrations within the first 90 days of go-live for customers on annual plans. We'll also provide a 30-day rollback window for configuration changes.

If useful, I can schedule a 30-minute technical call next week with our Okta integration engineer (Wed or Thu morning).

Regards,
Samir Patel
Enterprise Sales Engineer — Vanta
Vanta, Inc.
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.k@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.m@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.p@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.b@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SSO migration impact on our compliance platform shortlist

Team —

I pulled our retention policy and did a short risk review. Key security items:

- For TrustCenter's static service account approach, we must ensure the account is scoped to read-only event logs and rotated via a KMS-backed pipeline. I flagged this with infra; they prefer short-lived tokens (recommended).
- Both vendors support export of raw event data, but TrustCenter's export API is rate-limited; we need to confirm export SLAs if we plan to pull cold archives on demand.
- Data residency: not a blocker, but call out EU controls if we expand regions.

Recommendations:
1) Ask both vendors to provide an export SLA and an encryption-at-rest key rotation schedule.
2) Require PS cap language (max days + hourly cap) in the SOW to avoid surprise professional fees during migration.
3) Schedule the Vanta technical call — we should include one person from infra and one from security.

I'll draft language for legal to include; Laura, can you review the attached TrustCenter_service_terms_2027.pdf and flag any redlines?

-Neha
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.m@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.k@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.b@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.p@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.k@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 15:32:00 -0700
Subject: Decision ask: procurement path for compliance platform (Vanta vs TrustCenter)

Vivek / Laura —

Short summary and ask:
- SSO migration is scheduled mid-June to mid-July. Vanta has a cleaner Okta story and is offering a complimentary re-onboarding session; TrustCenter works but needs more PS time and has a reconfiguration fee in TS.
- Security wants export SLAs and token-rotation guarantees before committing. Legal should add a PS cap and a 30-day rollback window into any contract.
- Procurement impact: estimated incremental PS spend if we choose TrustCenter = ~5 days (approx $12k); Vanta PS estimate = ~3 days (approx $7k).

Decision requested: authorize procurement to sign a 12-month contract with the vendor that meets our security export SLA and includes a capped PS clause. If both meet it, prefer Vanta due to lower migration cost and faster SCIM alignment.

Requested by: 2027-05-21 COB (to meet vendor renewal windows).

Next steps I will take if approved:
- Kick off DocuSign with chosen vendor and route through finance.
- Schedule Vanta's technical session and invite infra/security.
- Track PS hours in the procurement P0 line item.

Thanks —
Rishi
Head of Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference
